free_tier.stated: No free tier. A residential dedicated IP is $19.99 per month, priced separately from the datacenter dedicated IP.
free_tier.notes: The unit of sale is the address, not a byte. The $19.99 buys one dedicated residential exit for a month, which is why no byte figure belongs in this field.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: The product is one exit address. Nothing is stored, so the largest-single-object question has no subject here.

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not stored bytes; how long one $19.99 payment holds the same address was not established
retention.notes: Address persistence policies across subscription renewal intervals are not stated in vendor documentation.

egress.terms: No traffic allowance or cap is published for the residential dedicated IP; the $19.99 per month is charged per address, so nothing read on 2026-10-24 prices traffic out per byte.

interface_detail: Reached as a tunnel exit by configuring VPN connection software with the assigned IP address. Web documentation paths returned HTTP 403 challenge pages on 2026-10-24. The cli interface token designates configuration files consumed by connection software.
tooling: A standard VPN client that consumes the config for the assigned address. Which protocols the residential product supports was not established, and no API for ordering or choosing the address was found. A missing wrapper is not a reason to reject an exit address; a tunnel client is all this shape needs.
chaining: One residential exit in front of the Workers AI gateway: the gateway keeps its Cloudflare identity, and only the traffic that must not originate from a datacenter egresses through this address.
limits_note: The one constraint found is the address count: $19.99 buys a single dedicated residential exit, so every request in the month presents from one IP and a second concurrent exit means a second subscription. No traffic allowance, request-rate figure or daily-volume limit was published in anything read on 2026-10-24, so no vocabulary kind carries a number here. Whether a fair-use ceiling exists is unstated, which is not the same as absent.
binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary fails at 45 GB/month across about 599,000 requests, which averages roughly 14 requests a minute: no traffic allowance and no request-rate figure is published to hit. The ceiling that arrives first is structural and outside the vocabulary, because one address is the entire product, so a block on that IP stops every request at once and there is no second exit to fail over to without a second $19.99 subscription.

identity_cost.detail: Card. There is no free tier, so the address is bought at $19.99 per month and a working card is what holds it. The facts name no second gate.

reliability_note: One address carries the reputation of everything sent through it, so a block hits all ~599,000 monthly requests at once and there is no second exit to fail over to.
confidence_note: Pricing and payment requirements are documented from vendor pages read on 2026-10-24. Marketing claims asserting residential ISP status could not be verified because server inventory paths returned HTTP 403 challenge pages and no public ASN lists are provided.

evidence.proved: A residential dedicated IP is sold at $19.99 per month and is priced separately from the datacenter dedicated IP; it is the cheapest per-address residential product found in this topic's research.

Two fetch paths in this session, curl with a browser user agent and the harness extractor, both returned HTTP 403 carrying the Cloudflare challenge text 'Just a moment...'. The server list and any ASN or ISP inventory were therefore unreadable, which is why the residential-origin claim stays unverified rather than quoted.

notes:
Product details for TorGuard dedicated residential IP add-ons. Marketing materials describe addresses as leased directly from major ISPs, but the vendor publishes no public ASN list, IP inventory, or test addresses. Furthermore, server listing pages returned HTTP 403 challenge pages on 2026-10-24, preventing automated inventory inspection. Consequently, the residential registration claim remains unverified against public registry databases.

Pricing and account gates: the dedicated residential IP is sold as an add-on requiring credit card payment during checkout. Standard plan cryptocurrency payment terms have not been verified for residential IP purchases. Bandwidth terms for the residential add-on are not stated explicitly on dedicated add-on pages.

extras.rung_note: The product is judged on its registration class, whether the address is announced by a consumer ISP or by a hosting provider, which is rung 5 rather than an ASN or a subnet.
extras.price_basis: per dedicated residential address, per month, priced separately from the datacenter dedicated IP
extras.comparison: cheapest per-address residential product found in this topic's research
extras.isp_claim_status: documented as a vendor statement, not checked against a registry: the vendor says the addresses are leased directly from major ISPs and terminate on servers it operates on bare metal in data centers, with the upstream ISP named for each US location (Spectrum, Sprint, AT&T, Windstream, Atlas); no per-address inventory or ASN is published, and the server list page returned no list.
extras.isp_claim_settled_by: one purchase plus one RIPE query on the assigned address
